standard_prerequisites.name: Nagata rings and finiteness of integral closures in finite extensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what makes the integral closure of B in a finite extension finite over B, the first step of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Valuation rings as maximal with respect to domination, and completeness of a finitely generated module over a complete ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies C with the integral closure of B in M and shows the auxiliary rings are complete.

standard_prerequisites.name: Inertia and ramification structure theory of extensions of discrete valuation rings
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: developed earlier in the same section and used throughout the rest of the counted proof span
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction to the totally ramified case in which the characteristic p machinery applies.

core_obligations: For any finite extension M' of L with integral closure C' of B, use that B is Nagata to conclude C' is finite over B, and that C' is a discrete valuation ring and complete as a B-module, hence complete as a discrete valuation ring (proof lines 35386-35392).
Conclude that the given C is the integral closure of B in M, by the defining maximality property of valuation rings with respect to domination (proof lines 35393-35395).
Reduce to the case in which M/L is totally ramified with respect to B, using the structure theory developed earlier in the section (rest of the counted proof span, source lines 35396-35511).

Apply the characteristic p input, available because k is algebraically closed of characteristic p and k is the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, to produce the required finite extension K_1/K (rest of the counted proof span).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a tower A in B in C of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L in M, assumes the residue field k of A algebraically closed of characteristic p > 0, that A and B are complete, that A -> B is weakly unramified, that M is a finite extension of L, and that k is the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, and concludes the existence of a finite extension K_1/K which is a weak solution for A -> C (source lines 35369-35383). The proof is long and is where the surrounding theory is assembled: it first establishes that the integral closure of B in any finite extension of L is a complete discrete valuation ring, using that B is Nagata and that the relevant rings are dominated by maximal ones, which also shows that C is the integral closure of B in M (proof lines 35386-35395). It then reduces to the case where M/L is totally ramified with respect to B, and proceeds through the structure theory of the inertia and ramification subgroups, the algebraically closed residue field, and the p-power residue hypothesis. The proof is a research-level synthesis: at every stage a generous reduction is required before the characteristic p input can be applied.
